scope: Six missing civil-rights detainees from Tallahassee and Albany, completing the 100-person accumulation.

core_letter.label: CORE-Lator, April 1960, no.81, pp.1-2: Patricia Stephens letter from Leon County Jail, named eight detainees, March 17 trial and 60-day sentence on inciting-to-riot count. Page1 and its letter enlarged and visually reviewed.

appleton.label: Clyde R. Appleton letter to the eight Tallahassee prisoners, April 28, 1960. State Archives of Florida, N2015-1, n2015-1_b001_f10_32. Full archival transcript and catalog identify all eight as jailed and identify Henry Marion Steele.

hirsch.label: Mildred Hirsch letter to Stephens, Angela Nance and Barbara Broxton, April 21, 1960. State Archives of Florida, N2015-1, n2015-1_b001_f10_33. Full transcript and catalog confirm ongoing confinement.

iowan_aug8.label: Jerry Elsea, SUI Student Jailed In Albany, The Daily Iowan, August 8, 1962, p.1. University of Iowa archive. Named July 21 jail entry, continued pretrial custody and city-ordinance charges; page visually reviewed.

iowan_aug9.label: The Daily Iowan, August 9, 1962, pp.1-2: Floyd Gardner hearing report and his smuggled July 27 letter. Page2 visually reviewed; feared five-year contempt exposure was not an imposed sentence.

prisoner.name: John Broxton
prisoner.description: John Broxton participated in the 1960 Tallahassee campaign against segregated lunch counters and the ensuing jail-in.

cases.charges: Inciting to riot — Tallahassee lunch-counter sit-in
cases.sentence: Sixty days or a $300 fine at the March 17, 1960 trial. Chose jail; correspondence confirms continued confinement at Leon County Jail on April 28. Exact release remains unverified.

entries.custody_evidence: Named in the April CORE jail letter and separately addressed as still jailed in the April 28 State Archives correspondence; custody continued over multiple weeks.

prisoner.name: Floyd Gardner
prisoner.description: Floyd Gardner was an Iowa student active in protests against racial discrimination. He joined the 1962 Albany, Georgia demonstrations and was held in the city jail awaiting trial.

cases.charges: Parading without a permit; violating traffic signals; obstructing traffic; congregating on sidewalks
cases.sentence: Held awaiting trial from July 21, 1962; still in Albany city jail in August 8-9 reporting. Individual sentence and exact release remain unverified.

entries.custody_evidence: Contemporary reporting dates jail entry to July 21; his letter mailed July 27 describes a week in jail without trial, and August reporting confirms continued confinement.

case_research.custody_evidence: Contemporary reporting dates jail entry to July 21; his letter mailed July 27 describes a week in jail without trial, and August reporting confirms continued confinement.

entries.status_research: The five-year contempt penalty feared in the letter was not imposed; the following editorial says the injunction was not in force at the arrest. Do not enter five years, a typical thirty-day penalty, or a projected hearing as an individual outcome. No CORE membership inferred. Historical custody is closed without asserting an exact release endpoint.

research_notes: Existing records untouched. Unverified birth/death dates, release dates, portraits and institution relations left unset. Case narrative names the documented jail.
